drawdown_context: MLKN entered the 2025-05-15 cutoff at $17.73 after a -42.8% drawdown from its trailing 52-week high. The drawdown reflects a real disclosed-distress event: in the Q3 FY25 10-Q filed 2025-03-31 the company recognized $92.3M of goodwill impairment (Global Retail $30.1M + Holly Hunt $62.2M) plus $37.7M of Knoll/Muuto trade-name impairment, posted an operating loss of -$82.2M for Q3 and a net loss attributable to MLKN of -$12.7M (-$0.19 EPS), simultaneously re-organized segments mid-quarter (creating a new 'Coverings' reporting unit with only a 10% goodwill cushion), and added new federal/DOGE risk-factor language (US federal government = ~4% of FY24 sales). The framework must judge whether the FY24 10-K -- filed nine months earlier -- showed disclosure tells that pre-staged this trajectory or whether management lied about it.

rfm_tuples.R: [FY24 10-K KPMG audit report, July 30, 2024]: 'We identified the evaluation of goodwill for impairment for the Global Retail reporting unit as a critical audit matter ... rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: claim_evolution. The MOST forensically important question on MLKN: a CAM is auditor code for 'we worried about this number.' KPMG flagged Global Retail goodwill ($391.8M) as a CAM in July 2024. Eight months later (Q3 FY25, filed 3/31/2025), management took $30.1M Global Retail + $62.2M Holly Hunt + $37.7M Knoll/Muuto trade-name impairment = $130M total. How did the FY24 cushion claim ('5% sales reduction would not result in impairment') survive?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 sensitivity table + Q3 FY25 10-Q Goodwill note (filed 3/31/2025)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 FY25 disclosure verbatim: 'management identified an impairment triggering event associated with lower-than-expected operating results ... the Company recognized a total non-cash impairment charge of $30.1 million and $62.2 million in its Global Retail and Holly Hunt reporting units, respectively. The goodwill impairment charges were primarily caused by reduced sales and profitability projections as well as an increase in the discount rate.' Plus $37.7M in Knoll+Muuto trade-name impairment. Total $130M. After this charge the surviving Global Retail/Holly Hunt goodwill was $357.0M + $33.0M = $390.0M (vs $391.8M at 6/1/24 -- essentially all the Knoll-acquisition Global Retail goodwill is now in question). The new Coverings reporting unit's cushion is only 10% post-reorg, with a disclosed $3.0M sensitivity to a 1% cash-flow decline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B claim evolution is unambiguous: the FY24 10-K's '5% sales reduction would not trigger impairment' was technically true at the test date but became false 8 months later when actual Global Retail / Holly Hunt operating results came in 'lower-than-expected.' Importantly, Q1 FY25 (-6.1% sales) and Q2 FY25 (+2.2% sales) 10-Qs each say 'No impairment triggering event' -- the trigger appeared in Q3 with the goodwill writedown ANNOUNCED at the same time as a mid-quarter segment re-organization that conveniently re-allocated Holly Hunt's remaining $33M of goodwill into Global Retail and created a brand-new 'Coverings' reporting unit (Maharam + Spinneybeck textiles) that already has only 10% cushion. The re-org has the effect of obscuring future Holly Hunt goodwill comparisons. This is the canonical 'restructure-the-segments-while-you-impair' tell.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Cumulative Knoll-related impairments by Q3 FY25: $36.7M (Americas Contract accumulated goodwill impairments pre-FY24) + $88.8M (Global Retail accumulated, pre-FY24) + $16.8M (Knoll+Muuto trade names in Q4 FY24) + $30.1M Global Retail + $62.2M Holly Hunt + $37.7M Knoll+Muuto = $272.3M of cumulative impairments traceable to the $1.8B Knoll-acquisition basket. Holly Hunt is a brand acquired through Knoll. The Knoll trade-name carrying value was $144.4M post-Q4-FY24 and was written down again in Q3 FY25 by $37.7M (Knoll + Muuto combined). summary: MillerKnoll is a NEGATIVE-LEAN survivor whose FY24 10-K disclosed enough Mode-B yellow flags to short the name from $35 down to $17 over the subsequent 9 months. The single most discriminating finding is claim_evolution on goodwill: KPMG named Global Retail goodwill ($391.8M) and Knoll/Muuto trade names (~$224M) as Critical Audit Matters in the July 2024 audit opinion; eight months later (Q3 FY25 10-Q filed 3/31/2025) management took $30.1M Global Retail + $62.2M Holly Hunt goodwill impairment plus $37.7M Knoll/Muuto trade-name impairment ($130M total) and posted an $82.2M operating loss. Both CAMs converted into impairments inside 8 months -- the auditor signaling worked. The Mode-B capital-allocation tell is equally damning: the Board upsized the buyback authorization by $200M on 7/16/2024 (two weeks before the 10-K with the CAM was filed); management then bought back $84.8M of stock at $25.81 avg through Q3 FY25, partly funded by drawing $24M on the revolver while EBITDA was deteriorating -- the canonical MGPI-style defend-the-price pattern. Insider-vs-calendar fires on the Baldwin 10b5-1 plan: Chris Baldwin (Group President with portfolio responsibility for the brands that bore the impairment) adopted a 101,462-share sale plan on 9/23/2024 -- 7 weeks after the FY24 10-K and 6 months before the Q3 impairment; no other officer adopted a plan in the entire 9-month pre-cutoff window. The dividend was frozen at $0.1875/quarter across all FY25 stub quarters (no raise, no cut -- the silent dog vs ANDE-comp which raised in the same window). The covenant story is in-compliance with high headroom but management refuses to publish the actual first-lien-net-leverage ratio number despite a 3.75x step-down through FY25. The Q3 segment re-organization (Holly Hunt moved into Global Retail, new Coverings unit with only 10% cushion) was timed concurrent with the impairment in a way that obscures future Holly Hunt comparability. Federal exposure (~4% of sales) was UNDERDISCLOSED in the 10-K as a concentration risk and only sized in the Q3 10-Q after the DOGE executive order. The drawdown to $17.73 was a REAL disclosed-distress event, not a sentiment markdown -- the framework should correctly assign MLKN a moderate-negative composite. Forward return of -12.9% confirms the call.
